info.title: Notion API
info.description: Notion API 2025-09-03 - Data Source Edition. Breaking change: Database endpoints replaced with data source endpoints.

id.description: The page's UUID. Pass it to API-retrieve-a-page, API-patch-page, or as a `block_id` to API-get-block-children.

icon.description: Emoji or file object, or null.

parent.description: One of `{type: "data_source_id", data_source_id}`, `{type: "page_id", page_id}`, `{type: "block_id", block_id}` or `{type: "workspace", workspace: true}`.

properties.description: Property values keyed by property name. Each value carries `id`, `type`, and the value itself under a key named by that type — so a select reads `{"type": "select", "select": {"name": ...}}`. A page outside a data source has only `title`.

public_url.description: Public share URL, or null when the page is not shared.

is_archived.description: Same state as `archived`, under the newer name.

request_id.description: Notion's id for this request. Quote it when reporting a problem to Notion.

blockObjectResponse.description: A block object. Its content sits under a key named by its own `type` — a paragraph carries `paragraph`, a heading `heading_1`.

parent.description: The page or block this one sits in.

type.description: The block type (`paragraph`, `heading_1`, `to_do`, `image`, `child_page`, ...), and also the name of the key holding this block's content.

has_children.description: True when the block contains child blocks; fetch them with API-get-block-children on this block's `id`.

paginatedListResponse.description: A paginated list. While `has_more` is true, pass `next_cursor` back as `start_cursor` to get the following page.

results.description: The items. Which object type they are follows `type` — page, block, data source, database, user or comment objects.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page, or null on the last one.

type.description: What `results` holds, e.g. `block`, `comment`, `user`, `page_or_data_source`. A key of that same name is also present, and is always an empty object.

dataSourceObjectResponse.description: A data source object — the column schema behind a database. Rows are pages; query them with API-query-data-source.

title.description: Rich text runs of the name.

properties.description: The column schema keyed by property name; each entry carries `id`, `name`, `type` and that type's own configuration, e.g. `select.options`. Read it before writing a page property — a select only accepts an option that already exists here.

parent.description: `{type: "database_id", database_id}` — the database this data source belongs to.

database_parent.description: Where that database itself lives, e.g. `{type: "page_id", page_id}`.

databaseObjectResponse.description: A database object. It holds presentation and the list of data sources; the columns live on the data source, not here.

data_sources.description: The database's data sources as `{id, name}`. Take an `id` from here and call API-retrieve-a-data-source or API-query-data-source with it — the database id itself cannot be queried for rows.

fileUploadObjectResponse.description: A file upload object. It is `pending` until the bytes arrive and `uploaded` afterwards, and it expires at `expiry_time` (one hour) unless it is attached to a block, page property or comment before then.

id.description: The upload id — send the bytes to it with API-send-a-file-upload, then reference it as `{"type": "file_upload", "file_upload": {"id": "<id>"}}`.

status.description: `pending` until the bytes arrive, then `uploaded`; also `expired` or `failed`.

content_length.description: How many bytes Notion stored — null while pending. Compare it with the source file's size: a smaller number means the payload was cut short on the way in.

upload_url.description: Where the bytes go. Present while the upload is pending.

expiry_time.description: When an unattached upload is discarded.

viewSortRequest.description: One sort rule applied to the view's rows. Same shape as a data source query sort.

property.description: Name or ID of the property to sort by.

viewFilterRequest.description: Filter applied to the view, using exactly the same shape as a data source query filter: either a single property condition (`{"property": "Status", "status": {"equals": "Done"}}`) or a compound `{"and": [...]}` / `{"or": [...]}`. Notion validates each value against the property's configured options, and for status properties it also accepts group names, so an invalid value comes back as a descriptive error listing what is available. Send `null` on update to clear the filter entirely.

viewGroupSortRequest.description: Order the groups themselves are listed in — distinct from `sorts`, which orders rows inside a group.

type.description: `manual` keeps the order the options are defined in (for a status or select property this is the order shown in the Notion UI), which is usually what you want for a workflow board.

viewGroupByRequest.description: How rows or cards are grouped — board columns, or sections in a table. Which extra fields apply is decided by `type`, which must match the grouped property's own type. `select`, `multi_select`, `person`, `created_by`, `last_edited_by`, `relation` and `checkbox` take no extra field. `status` requires `group_by`: `group` (To-do / In progress / Complete) or `option` (one column per individual option). `date`, `created_time` and `last_edited_time` require `group_by` (`relative` | `day` | `week` | `month` | `year`) and may set `start_day_of_week`. `text`, `title`, `url`, `email` and `phone_number` require `group_by`: `exact` or `alphabet_prefix`. `number` may set `range_start` / `range_end` / `range_size` to bucket values. `formula` requires `group_by` to be a nested object describing the formula's result type (`{"type": "number", "sort": {...}, "range_size": 10}`) without a `property_id` of its own.

type.description: The type of the property being grouped by.

property_id.description: ID of the property to group by. A property name is also accepted and resolved to its ID.

hide_empty_groups.description: Whether groups with no items are hidden. Notion defaults this to `true` when grouping is (re)applied, which silently hides a column such as an empty `Open` status — set it explicitly to `false` to keep every group visible so a card can still be dragged into an empty one.

group_by.description: Required for `status`, `date`/`created_time`/`last_edited_time`, text-like and `formula` types; see this schema's description for the value each one takes. A string for every type except `formula`, which takes a nested group-by object.

anyOf.description: Formula-only nested grouping: `type` is the formula's result type (`date`, `text`, `number` or `checkbox`) plus that type's own fields and a `sort`. It carries no `property_id` — that is inherited from the parent.

start_day_of_week.description: Which day a week starts on when grouping dates by week: 0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday.

range_start.description: Number grouping only: lower bound of the first bucket.

range_end.description: Number grouping only: upper bound of the last bucket.

range_size.description: Number grouping only: width of each bucket.

viewPropertyConfigRequest.description: Visibility and display of a single property in this view. The order of the entries in the `properties` array is the order the columns or card fields appear in, so reordering the array reorders the view.

property_id.description: The property's ID, or its name — a name is resolved to the matching ID. If a string matches both one property's ID and a different property's name, the ID wins.

visible.description: Whether the property is shown in this view.

width.description: Column width in pixels. Table views only.

wrap.description: Whether the value wraps onto multiple lines in its cell or card.

status_show_as.description: How a status property is rendered.

card_property_width_mode.description: Width behaviour of this property on compact board or gallery cards.

date_format.description: Display format for a date property.

time_format.description: Time display format for a date property.

viewPropertiesRequest.description: Which properties are visible and in what order. Array order is display order.

viewCoverRequest.description: Where the image at the top of each board or gallery card comes from.

type.description: `page_cover` uses the page's own cover, `page_content` the first image in the page body, `property` an image held in a file property named by `property_id`.

property_id.description: File property to take the image from. Only meaningful when `type` is `property`.

viewSubtaskConfigRequest.description: How parent/child rows nest in a table view, via a self-referencing relation property.

property_id.description: The self-referencing relation property that establishes the hierarchy.

display_mode.description: `show` nests with toggles, `hidden` shows parents with a count, `flattened` lists sub-items with a parent indicator, `disabled` turns sub-item rendering off.

filter_scope.description: Which rows the view's filter is applied to.

toggle_column_id.description: Property whose column carries the expand/collapse toggle.

viewChartAggregationRequest.description: How values are aggregated for a chart axis or a number chart.

aggregator.description: `count` counts rows and needs no `property_id`; every other operator requires one.

property_id.description: Property to aggregate. Required for every aggregator except `count`.

viewConfigurationRequest.description: Layout settings for the view. This is a union discriminated on `type`, and that `type` must equal the view's own `type`. When updating, send only the fields you want changed — anything omitted is left alone, and a nullable field set to `null` is cleared.

subtasks.description: Sub-item display. `null` resets to defaults; use `{"display_mode": "disabled"}` to actually switch it off.

frozen_column_index.description: How many columns stay pinned on the left when scrolling.

show_vertical_lines.description: Whether vertical grid lines are drawn between columns.

group_by.description: What the board's columns are. Required for a board view — a board cannot exist without grouping.

sub_group_by.description: Optional second level of grouping within each column. `null` removes it.

cover_size.description: Card size — how large the cover image is on each card.

cover_aspect.description: `contain` fits the whole image, `cover` fills the card area and crops.

card_layout.description: `list` shows full cards, `compact` is the condensed card layout.

cover_size.description: Card size — how large the cover image is on each card.

cover_aspect.description: `contain` fits the whole image, `cover` fills the card area and crops.

card_layout.description: `list` shows full cards, `compact` is the condensed card layout.

date_property_id.description: Date property that positions each item on the calendar.
Date property giving each item its start.

end_date_property_id.description: Date property giving each item its end. `null` clears it.

show_table.description: Whether the table panel is shown beside the timeline.

preference.description: Zoom and centring of the timeline.

center_timestamp.description: Milliseconds since the epoch to centre the timeline on.

arrows_by.description: Relation property drawn as dependency arrows. `{"property_id": null}` or `null` disables arrows.

color_by.description: Whether items are coloured by a property.

map_by.description: Location property used to place each pin.

is_form_closed.description: Whether the form has stopped accepting submissions.

anonymous_submissions.description: Whether people who are not logged in may submit.

submission_permissions.description: What access the submitter keeps on the page their submission creates.

oneOf.title: Chart
oneOf.description: Charts read data either as grouped data (`x_axis` + `y_axis`) or as raw property values (`x_axis_property_id` + `y_axis_property_id`); use one pair or the other.

chart_type.description: `column` is vertical bars, `bar` horizontal, `number` a single aggregated value.

x_axis.description: Grouping for the x axis, same shape as `group_by`. `null` clears it.

x_axis_property_id.description: Property supplying x values in raw-results mode.

y_axis_property_id.description: Property supplying y values in raw-results mode.

stack_by.description: Second grouping for stacked or side-by-side column, bar and line charts.

hide_empty_groups.description: Whether x-axis groups with no data are hidden.

color_by_value.description: Bar and column charts only: shade each bar along a gradient by its value.

group_style.description: Bar and column charts only: `normal` stacks, `percent` normalises to 100%, `side_by_side` places bars next to each other.

reference_lines.description: Horizontal lines drawn at fixed y values for comparison.

oneOf.title: Dashboard
oneOf.description: A dashboard's layout is read-only: it is returned when retrieving the view, but cannot be set here. Build a dashboard by creating widget views against it — call create-a-view with `view_id` set to the dashboard's ID.

blockTextUpdateRequest.description: The new text for a block that holds text. Used by API-update-a-block under the key naming the block's own type.

rich_text.description: The block's new text, as one or more runs. It replaces the block's existing text completely, so send the whole corrected line and not just the changed part — an empty array clears the block's text.

toDoBlockUpdateRequest.description: The new state of a to-do block. Send `rich_text`, `checked`, or both — whichever is left out keeps its current value.

rich_text.description: The to-do's new text, replacing the existing text completely. Leave it out to tick or untick the box without touching the wording.

imageBlockRequest.description: An image block. Use `external` for a publicly reachable URL, or `file_upload` for bytes uploaded via API-create-a-file-upload + API-send-a-file-upload.

url.description: Publicly reachable image URL. Notion fetches it, so it must not require authentication.

id.description: The `id` from API-create-a-file-upload, after the bytes were sent with API-send-a-file-upload.

fileBlockRequest.description: A file attachment block (PDF, zip, ...). Same two sources as an image block.

id.description: The `id` from API-create-a-file-upload, after the bytes were sent with API-send-a-file-upload.

get.description: List the views of a database, or every view that reads a given data source. Pass `database_id` for the views shown as tabs on one database, or `data_source_id` to also pick up linked views of that data source living on other pages across the workspace. Results only include views the integration can access. Each entry is a reference carrying just `object` and `id` — call Retrieve a view for a view's filter, sorts and layout.

parameters.name: database_id
parameters.description: The database whose views to list. This is the database container's ID, not a data source ID. At least one of `database_id` or `data_source_id` is required.

parameters.name: data_source_id
parameters.description: List every view reading this data source, including linked views on other pages. At least one of `database_id` or `data_source_id` is required.

parameters.name: start_cursor
parameters.description: Return the page of results starting after this cursor.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Number of items to return. Maximum 100, default 100.

parameters.name: Notion-Version
parameters.description: The Notion API version. The view endpoints require 2025-09-03 or later; this server pins 2026-03-11, the version Notion's own view documentation is written against.

post.description: Create a view over a data source: a table, board, calendar, timeline, gallery, list, form, chart, map or dashboard, with its own filter, sorts and layout. Exactly one of `database_id`, `view_id` or `create_database` must be given — `database_id` adds a tab to an existing database, `view_id` adds a widget to an existing dashboard, and `create_database` puts a linked view of an existing data source on a page. Note that `database_id` and `data_source_id` are different IDs and both are needed: retrieve the database to find its `data_sources` array. `configuration.type` must equal the view's `type`, and a board view must carry a `group_by`.

parameters.name: Notion-Version
parameters.description: The Notion API version. The view endpoints require 2025-09-03 or later; this server pins 2026-03-11, the version Notion's own view documentation is written against.

data_source_id.description: The data source the view reads. Found in the `data_sources` array of the database object — not the same as `database_id`.

name.description: Display name of the view, shown on its tab.

type.description: The view's layout. `configuration.type` must match this.

database_id.description: Create the view as a tab on this database. Mutually exclusive with `view_id` and `create_database`.

view_id.description: Add the view as a widget to this dashboard view. Mutually exclusive with `database_id` and `create_database`.

create_database.description: Put a linked view of an existing data source on a page, creating a lightweight database container there. Unlike creating a database, no new schema is made — the view points at a data source another database owns, so the integration needs access to both. Mutually exclusive with `database_id` and `view_id`.

parent.description: The page to place the linked database on, as `{"type": "page_id", "page_id": "..."}`.

position.description: Where in the page the database block goes. `{"type": "after_block", "block_id": "..."}` places it after a block that is a direct child of the parent page. Defaults to the end of the page.

sorts.description: Sort rules for the view's rows.

quick_filters.description: Filters offered in the view's filter bar, as a map from property name or ID to a filter condition written without its `property` field — for example `{"Status": {"status": {"equals": "In progress"}}}`. A people filter accepts `"me"` as its value, so "assigned to me" needs no user ID.

position.description: Where the new tab sits in the view bar. `{"type": "start"}`, `{"type": "end"}` (the default), or `{"type": "after_view", "view_id": "..."}`. Only valid together with `database_id`.

placement.description: Where the new widget sits in a dashboard. `{"type": "new_row"}` appends a row, `{"type": "new_row", "row_index": 0}` inserts one, `{"type": "existing_row", "row_index": 2}` joins an existing row (maximum 4 widgets per row). Only valid together with `view_id`.

get.description: Retrieve one view in full: its name, type, filter, sorts, quick filters and layout configuration. This is the only way to read a view's settings — List views returns bare `id` references. Retrieving a dashboard returns its layout, the rows of widgets with their view IDs, widths and row indexes.

parameters.name: view_id
parameters.description: Identifier for a Notion view.

parameters.name: Notion-Version
parameters.description: The Notion API version. The view endpoints require 2025-09-03 or later; this server pins 2026-03-11, the version Notion's own view documentation is written against.

patch.description: Change a view's name, filter, sorts, quick filters or layout. Every field is optional and anything omitted is left as it was, so a partial update is safe. To remove a setting, send it as `null` — `filter: null` drops the filter, `configuration: {"type": "table", "group_by": null}` ungroups a table. Sending a `quick_filters` entry replaces just that one and leaves the rest; setting an entry to `null` removes it. `configuration.type` must match the view's existing type. Note that re-applying grouping resets `hide_empty_groups` to true, so set it explicitly to false in the same call if empty groups must stay visible.

parameters.name: view_id
parameters.description: Identifier for a Notion view.

parameters.name: Notion-Version
parameters.description: The Notion API version. The view endpoints require 2025-09-03 or later; this server pins 2026-03-11, the version Notion's own view documentation is written against.

name.description: New display name for the view.

filter.description: Replaces the view's filter. `null` clears it.

sorts.description: Replaces the view's sort rules. `null` clears them.

quick_filters.description: Adds or replaces individual entries in the filter bar, keyed by property name or ID; entries you do not mention are kept. Set one entry to `null` to remove it, or the whole object to `null` to clear the bar.

delete.description: Permanently remove a view from its database. This cannot be undone through the API. A database must keep at least one view, so deleting the last one fails with a validation error — to get rid of the database itself, set `in_trash` on the database instead. The response is a partial view object with only `object`, `id`, `parent` and `type`, since the view no longer exists to describe.

parameters.name: view_id
parameters.description: Identifier for a Notion view.

parameters.name: Notion-Version
parameters.description: The Notion API version. The view endpoints require 2025-09-03 or later; this server pins 2026-03-11, the version Notion's own view documentation is written against.

post.description: Run a view's saved filter and sort and get the first page of matching pages back, so you see what a person looking at that view sees without rebuilding its filter logic yourself. The response carries the results plus a `query_id`, `total_count` and `has_more`; use Get view query results with that `query_id` to page through the rest. The cached result set expires on its own after about 15 minutes.

parameters.name: view_id
parameters.description: Identifier for a Notion view.

parameters.name: Notion-Version
parameters.description: The Notion API version. The view endpoints require 2025-09-03 or later; this server pins 2026-03-11, the version Notion's own view documentation is written against.

page_size.description: How many results to return in this first page. Maximum 100.

get.description: Fetch a further page from a result set already produced by Create a view query, using the `query_id` it returned. Pass the previous response's `next_cursor` as `start_cursor`. The cached set expires after about 15 minutes, after which the query has to be created again.

parameters.name: view_id
parameters.description: Identifier for a Notion view.

parameters.name: query_id
parameters.description: The `id` returned by Create a view query.

parameters.name: start_cursor
parameters.description: Continue from this cursor, taken from the previous response's `next_cursor`.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: How many results to return. Maximum 100.

parameters.name: Notion-Version
parameters.description: The Notion API version. The view endpoints require 2025-09-03 or later; this server pins 2026-03-11, the version Notion's own view documentation is written against.

delete.description: Release a cached view query once you have finished paging through it. Optional housekeeping — a query expires by itself after about 15 minutes — but worth doing when queries are run often. It deletes only the cached result set; the view and its pages are untouched.

parameters.name: view_id
parameters.description: Identifier for a Notion view.

parameters.name: query_id
parameters.description: The `id` returned by Create a view query.

parameters.name: Notion-Version
parameters.description: The Notion API version. The view endpoints require 2025-09-03 or later; this server pins 2026-03-11, the version Notion's own view documentation is written against.

post.description: Step 1 of attaching a file to Notion. Reserves an upload and returns an `id`. Then call `API-send-a-file-upload` with that id to transfer the bytes, and finally reference it from a block or property as `{"type": "file_upload", "file_upload": {"id": "<id>"}}`. Single-part uploads are limited to 20MB. An upload must be attached within one hour or it expires.

filename.description: Name of the file including its extension, e.g. 'screenshot.png'. Determines the name shown in Notion. Required when mode is 'external_url'.

content_type.description: MIME type, e.g. 'image/png'. Inferred from the filename when omitted.

mode.description: 'single_part' (default, up to 20MB), 'multi_part' for larger files, or 'external_url' to have Notion import a publicly reachable file itself.

external_url.description: Only with mode 'external_url'. HTTPS URL of a publicly accessible file for Notion to import. The import is asynchronous: the upload starts as 'pending', so poll API-retrieve-a-file-upload until it reports 'uploaded' before attaching it.

post.description: Step 2: transfer the bytes for an upload created by `API-create-a-file-upload`. Because this server runs remotely and shares no filesystem with the caller, the `file` parameter accepts a data: URI, a bare base64 string, or an http(s) URL the server can fetch — a local path only works when running over stdio. Whichever form is used, the whole file travels in this one call as a single unbroken payload: contents produced in pieces must be joined before they are sent, and `content_length` is what proves none went missing.

parameters.name: file_upload_id
parameters.description: The `id` returned by API-create-a-file-upload.

file.description: File contents as a data: URI, a bare base64 string, or an http(s) URL to fetch. Send them as one continuous, unbroken string in a single call. Contents assembled in pieces — chunked reads, several tool calls, an encoder that emitted parts — must be joined first: a payload that lost a piece on the way still decodes cleanly and looks whole, so the loss is caught only by the `content_length` check, and only if you sent it.

content_length.description: Size of the source file in bytes, before encoding. Always send it. Encoded contents can be cut short on the way here and still look well-formed, in which case Notion stores the fragment and reports success; this number is compared against what actually arrived and the upload is refused on any mismatch. Without it, a payload whose completeness cannot be established from its own bytes is refused rather than stored.

filename.description: Optional name for the multipart part; defaults to the create step's filename.

get.description: Check the status of a file upload ('pending', 'uploaded', 'expired', 'failed').

parameters.name: file_upload_id
parameters.description: Identifier for a file upload.

parameters.name: start_cursor
parameters.description: If supplied, this endpoint will return a page of results starting after the cursor provided. If not supplied, this endpoint will return the first page of results.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: The number of items from the full list desired in the response. Maximum: 100

query.description: The text that the API compares page and database titles against.

sort.description: A set of criteria, `direction` and `timestamp` keys, that orders the results. The **only** supported timestamp value is `"last_edited_time"`. Supported `direction` values are `"ascending"` and `"descending"`. If `sort` is not provided, then the most recently edited results are returned first.

direction.description: The direction to sort. Possible values include `ascending` and `descending`.

timestamp.description: The name of the timestamp to sort against. Possible values include `last_edited_time`.

filter.description: A set of criteria, `value` and `property` keys, that limits the results to either only pages or only data sources. Possible `value` values are `"page"` or `"data_source"`. The only supported `property` value is `"object"`.

value.description: The value of the property to filter the results by.  Possible values for object type include `page` or `data_source`.  **Limitation**: Currently the only filter allowed is `object` which will filter by type of object (either `page` or `data_source`)

property.description: The name of the property to filter by. Currently the only property you can filter by is the object type.  Possible values include `object`.   Limitation: Currently the only filter allowed is `object` which will filter by type of object (either `page` or `data_source`)

start_cursor.description: A `cursor` value returned in a previous response that If supplied, limits the response to results starting after the `cursor`. If not supplied, then the first page of results is returned. Refer to [pagination](https://developers.notion.com/reference/intro#pagination) for more details.

page_size.description: The number of items from the full list to include in the response. Maximum: `100`.

parameters.name: block_id
parameters.description: Identifier for a [block](ref:block)

parameters.name: start_cursor
parameters.description: If supplied, this endpoint will return a page of results starting after the cursor provided. If not supplied, this endpoint will return the first page of results.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: The number of items from the full list desired in the response. Maximum: 100

parameters.name: block_id
parameters.description: Identifier for a [block](ref:block). Also accepts a [page](ref:page) ID.

children.description: Child content to append to a container block as an array of [block objects](ref:block)

after.description: The ID of the existing block that the new block should be appended after.

parameters.name: block_id
parameters.description: Identifier for a Notion block

patch.summary: Correct the text of a block that is already on a page. Pass the one property named after the block's own type — `paragraph`, `bulleted_list_item`, `to_do`, `heading_1` and so on — carrying the new `rich_text`. The new `rich_text` replaces the block's existing text entirely, so send the whole corrected line and not just the changed part. Notion only lets an existing block's text (and `checked`, on a `to_do`) be updated; a block cannot be turned into another type this way. Editing in place keeps the block's id, its position on the page and any comments anchored to it — appending a corrected copy and archiving the old one does not.
patch.description: Send exactly one block-type property. It goes at the top level of the request body, beside `archived`, in the same shape API-patch-block-children uses for a new block: `{"paragraph": {"rich_text": [{"text": {"content": "…"}}]}}`. There is no wrapper object around it — an earlier version of this spec had one, and Notion answered every such call with a validation error naming each block type as undefined.

parameters.name: block_id
parameters.description: Identifier for a Notion block

schema.description: The block's new content. Send the single property whose name matches the block's existing type — retrieve the block first with API-retrieve-a-block if the type is unknown. A key that names a different type is rejected with a 400 `validation_error` reading "Block type mismatch", because a block cannot be changed into another type; to replace a block with one of another type, append the new block with API-patch-block-children and archive the old one.

archived.description: Set to true to archive (delete) a block. Set to false to un-archive (restore) a block. Leave it out when editing text — it is not needed for an edit and archiving is a separate action.

parameters.name: block_id
parameters.description: Identifier for a Notion block

parameters.name: page_id
parameters.description: Identifier for a Notion page

parameters.name: filter_properties
parameters.description: A list of page property value IDs associated with the page. Use this param to limit the response to a specific page property value or values. To retrieve multiple properties, specify each page property ID. For example: `?filter_properties=iAk8&filter_properties=b7dh`.

parameters.name: page_id
parameters.description: The identifier for the Notion page to be updated.

properties.description: The property values to update for the page. The keys are the names or IDs of the property and the values are property values. If a page property ID is not included, then it is not changed.

in_trash.description: Set to true to delete a block. Set to false to restore a block.

icon.description: A page icon for the page. Supported types are [external file object](https://developers.notion.com/reference/file-object) or [emoji object](https://developers.notion.com/reference/emoji-object).

cover.description: A cover image for the page. Only [external file objects](https://developers.notion.com/reference/file-object) are supported.

properties.description: The property values for the new page. The keys are the names or IDs of the property and the values are property values.

children.description: The content to be rendered on the new page, represented as an array of [block objects](https://developers.notion.com/reference/block). Cannot be combined with `markdown`.

markdown.description: The whole page body as Notion-flavoured Markdown, written while the page is created — no follow-up append call. Mutually exclusive with `children`.

icon.description: The icon of the new page. Either an [emoji object](https://developers.notion.com/reference/emoji-object) or an [external file object](https://developers.notion.com/reference/file-object)..

cover.description: The cover image of the new page, represented as a [file object](https://developers.notion.com/reference/file-object).

parameters.description: Identifier for a page [property](https://developers.notion.com/reference/page#all-property-values)

get.description: Retrieves a list of un-resolved [Comment objects](ref:comment-object) from a page or block.

parameters.name: block_id
parameters.description: Identifier for a Notion block or page

parameters.name: start_cursor
parameters.description: If supplied, this endpoint will return a page of results starting after the cursor provided. If not supplied, this endpoint will return the first page of results.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: The number of items from the full list desired in the response. Maximum: 100

parameters.name: created_after
parameters.description: Return only comments created strictly after this moment, as an ISO-8601 date-time (e.g. `2026-08-10T03:11:00.000Z`). Answers "has anything been said since I last looked?" in one call, instead of re-reading the thread from its first comment every time. Pass the `created_time` of the newest comment you have already seen. NOTE: this is not a parameter of Notion's API — Notion offers no sort or filter on comments — it is performed by this server, which walks the thread with `start_cursor` and returns the matching comments in the ordinary list envelope (`has_more` false, `next_cursor` null). Two consequences: the cost is paid server-side rather than saved outright, and past 2000 comments the call fails rather than answer from a partial scan. Notion records comment times to the minute, so a comment made in the same minute as the timestamp you pass is treated as older and left out; pass the newest `created_time` you hold and accept a re-read of that minute if you cannot miss one.

post.description: Creates a comment in a page or existing discussion thread.

parent.description: What the comment is attached to: a page or a single block. Omit when replying into an existing thread with `discussion_id`.

oneOf.description: Comment anchored to one block, e.g. a paragraph, heading or to-do item.

block_id.description: the block ID the comment is attached to

discussion_id.description: Reply into an existing discussion thread instead of starting a new one. Take it from the `discussion_id` of a comment returned by API-retrieve-a-comment. Cannot be combined with `parent`.

rich_text.description: The comment's text, as one or more runs. Notion caps each run's `text.content` at 2000 characters and the array at 100 runs — the cap is per run, not per comment, so a message longer than 2000 characters goes into several runs here rather than being cut. Over the limit the whole call fails with a 400 validation error, so split long text before sending it.

content.description: The content of this run of the comment. Maximum 2000 characters; a longer one is rejected with a 400. Continue past 2000 characters in the next entry of `rich_text` — the runs are joined into a single comment.

attachments.description: Files to attach to the comment, e.g. a screenshot. Upload the bytes first with API-create-a-file-upload + API-send-a-file-upload, then reference the upload id here. Maximum 3.

file_upload_id.description: The `id` from API-create-a-file-upload, after the bytes were sent with API-send-a-file-upload.

display_name.description: Who the comment is signed as. Omitted, it is signed with the integration's own name - the same name for everyone sharing this token, so on a busy page every author looks alike. Pass `{"type": "custom", "custom": {"name": "..."}}` to sign it with the individual agent or person posting instead. Applies to this comment only; it sets no default for later ones.

type.description: `custom` shows the name given in `custom.name` - the only value that carries a name of your choosing, and the one to use for signing as an agent. `user` shows the person who authorised the token. `integration` and `connection` are two names for the same thing, the integration itself, which is also what you get by omitting `display_name` entirely.

custom.description: The name to sign with. Required when `type` is `custom`, and meaningless otherwise.

name.description: The label shown as the comment's author, e.g. the name of the agent posting. Free text - it is not resolved against Notion users, and confers no identity or permission.

delete.summary: Delete a comment permanently. This cannot be undone — a deleted comment is gone for good, with no trash to restore it from. Deletes exactly one comment, named by its id.

parameters.name: comment_id
parameters.description: The id of the one comment to delete. Take it from the `id` of a comment returned by API-retrieve-a-comment — not its `discussion_id`, which names the whole thread and cannot be deleted in one call. Deletion is permanent and irreversible: there is no undo and no way to read the comment back afterwards, so confirm the id is the intended comment before calling. Only comments this integration itself created can be deleted; someone else's comment answers 404.

403.description: Forbidden — the integration lacks the insert-comment capability

404.description: Not found — no such comment, or it was created by someone else

patch.summary: Correct a comment that is already posted. Replaces its text in place, so the comment keeps its position in the thread instead of having to be deleted and written again. The new text replaces the old one entirely — there is no way to append to a comment.

parameters.name: comment_id
parameters.description: The id of the one comment to correct. Take it from the `id` of a comment returned by API-retrieve-a-comment — not its `discussion_id`, which names the whole thread. Only comments this integration itself created can be edited; someone else's comment answers 404.

rich_text.description: The comment's new text, as one or more runs. It replaces the existing text completely, so send the whole corrected comment and not just the changed part. Notion caps each run's `text.content` at 2000 characters and the array at 100 runs — the cap is per run, not per comment, so text longer than 2000 characters goes into several runs here.

content.description: The content of this run of the comment. Maximum 2000 characters; a longer one is rejected with a 400. Continue past 2000 characters in the next entry of `rich_text` — the runs are joined into a single comment.

403.description: Forbidden — the integration lacks the insert-comment capability

404.description: Not found — no such comment, or it was created by someone else

patch.summary: Update a page's content as Markdown
patch.description: Update the content of a Notion page using enhanced Markdown. Prefer `replace_content` to overwrite the whole page or `update_content` for targeted find-and-replace edits.

parameters.name: page_id
parameters.description: Identifier for a Notion page (or block) to read or update as markdown.

parameters.name: Notion-Version
parameters.description: The Notion API version. The page-markdown endpoints require 2026-03-11 or later.

schema.description: Specify exactly one edit operation. Set `type` to the operation name and provide the matching object.

type.description: The kind of edit to apply. Prefer `replace_content` (overwrite the whole page) or `update_content` (targeted find-and-replace). `insert_content` and `replace_content_range` are deprecated.

replace_content.description: Provide when type is `replace_content`. Replaces the entire page content.

new_str.description: The complete new page content as enhanced Markdown.

allow_deleting_content.description: Permit deletion of existing child pages/databases that are no longer present in the new content.

update_content.description: Provide when type is `update_content`. Applies targeted find-and-replace edits.

content_updates.description: Up to 100 find-and-replace edits applied in order.

old_str.description: Exact existing Markdown text to find.

replace_all_matches.description: Replace every occurrence of old_str instead of just the first (default false).

allow_deleting_content.description: Permit deletion of existing child pages/databases removed by the edits.

insert_content.description: Deprecated. Provide when type is `insert_content`. Inserts Markdown at a position.

after.description: Ellipsis-format selection ("start text...end text") to insert after. Cannot be combined with position.

position.description: Insert at the start or end of the page. Cannot be combined with after.

replace_content_range.description: Deprecated. Provide when type is `replace_content_range`. Replaces a selected range of Markdown.

content.description: New Markdown content for the range.

content_range.description: Ellipsis-format selection ("start text...end text") identifying the range to replace.

allow_deleting_content.description: Permit deletion of child pages/databases within the replaced range.

id.description: ID of the page or block.

markdown.description: Page content rendered as enhanced Markdown.

truncated.description: True if content was truncated because the page exceeds the block limit.

unknown_block_ids.description: Block IDs that could not be rendered (e.g. due to permissions or truncation). Pass them back to this endpoint to fetch them individually.
